dataset: Who can reach it out of the box: default network and account settings of self-hosted AI tools, read from each project's own source and docs
license: CC BY 4.0 for this file; each project keeps its own licence
purpose: California's SB 574 (Business and Professions Code section 6068.1, from 1 January 2027) turns on whether access to what an attorney enters into a generative AI system is restricted to the attorney and authorised persons. For a self-hosted setup that depends on software settings. This file records, for each tool, what those settings are before anyone changes them. It is a record of software defaults, not a legal conclusion about any office.

fields.role: model_server (answers prompts over an Ollama-style or OpenAI-style API, itself or by forwarding to other model servers) | chat_app (web front end with accounts and stored chat history)
fields.release_seen: latest release tag on the project's GitHub releases page on the checked date, as the project writes it (with or without a leading v); the source files were read from the default branch the same day
fields.listen_direct: the address the program listens on when started with no options
fields.listen_container: the address in the project's own container image, compose file or documented Docker command, or null if MV2 did not check one
fields.credential_by_default: none = the API or app answers without any login or key | key = the API answers only with a key, and the program will not start without one | login = the app requires an account
fields.credential_options: what the project offers to require a key or login
fields.signup_default: for chat apps, whether someone who can reach the app can create an account, or null for model servers
fields.other_defaults: other defaults that bear on who can read what is entered, or null
fields.out_of_the_box: one sentence: who can use the tool or read what is entered, as shipped
fields.sources: the source files and documentation pages the facts were read from
fields.notes: limits of the check, or null

entries.listen_container: port 3001 published on every host interface by the standard install command
entries.credential_options: Password Protect Instance (single user) or Multi-User Mode with admin, manager and default roles, both switched on under Settings > Security
entries.signup_default: no accounts exist until Multi-User Mode is turned on; before that there is no login at all
entries.other_defaults: In single-user mode anyone with the instance password can change every setting and view all chats.
entries.out_of_the_box: Anyone who can reach port 3001 on the host can use the app, change its settings and read its workspaces and chats.
entries.notes: Read from the project's documentation, which states that a local instance has no authentication by default and that the standard Docker command binds port 3001 to every interface. The desktop app was not checked.

entries.listen_container: ports 80 and 443 published on every host interface by the nginx service (EXPOSE_NGINX_PORT=80 and EXPOSE_NGINX_SSL_PORT=443 in docker/.env.example); the plugin daemon's debugging port 5003 is also published
entries.credential_options: email and password login (ENABLE_EMAIL_PASSWORD_LOGIN=True); email-code login and GitHub/Google login are off by default; INIT_PASSWORD, when set, gates the one-time /install page
entries.signup_default: closed once set up: ALLOW_REGISTER=False and ALLOW_CREATE_WORKSPACE=False, so new members come by workspace invitation; but INIT_PASSWORD is empty, so until the first admin exists whoever opens /install first creates the admin account
entries.other_defaults: Setup refuses to run again once a setup time is recorded or any workspace exists (api/services/setup_service.py), so the open /install window closes when the first admin is created.
entries.out_of_the_box: After setup only invited members can sign in; before it, anyone who can reach port 80 can open /install and make themselves the workspace owner, because no setup password is set by default.
entries.notes: Read from the default branch; the 1.17.1 tag was not compared. That /install asks for no password when INIT_PASSWORD is empty comes from the project's documentation ('If you set it, the /install page asks for this password'); the code that turns INIT_PASSWORD into the validation-required flag was not read. What the plugin debugging port accepts was not checked.

entries.credential_options: email and password accounts; social and OpenID logins are off by default
entries.signup_default: open: ALLOW_REGISTRATION=true, and ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_EMAIL_LOGIN=true lets a new account sign in without a verified address
entries.other_defaults: ALLOW_SHARED_LINKS=true (users can create share links to chats); ALLOW_SHARED_LINKS_PUBLIC=false (viewers must be logged in).
entries.out_of_the_box: With the shipped compose file, anyone who can reach the port can register an account and use the app; each user sees their own chats, and shared links open to any logged-in user.
entries.notes: Values are those in the example environment file that the install instructions copy to .env; an operator who edits .env before first start changes them.

entries.listen_container: port 4000 published on every host interface (docker-compose.yml maps "4000:4000"); the same file also publishes its Postgres database on 5432, with a fixed password written in the file, and Prometheus on 9090
entries.credential_options: a master key (LITELLM_MASTER_KEY, empty in .env.example) and virtual keys issued under it; JWT, OAuth2 and OAuth2-proxy authentication can be switched on in general_settings
entries.other_defaults: The proxy refuses to start when the master key is unset, empty or a publicly known default (litellm/proxy/auth/master_key_boot_check.py), whatever address it listens on. LITELLM_DANGEROUSLY_PERMIT_WEAK_OR_UNSET_MASTER_KEY=true, or dangerously_permit_weak_or_unset_master_key in general_settings, overrides that for local development; with the override on and no master key, every request is accepted as an internal user (litellm/proxy/auth/user_api_key_auth.py).
entries.out_of_the_box: It listens on every interface, but it will not start until someone sets a master key that is neither empty nor a known default, so no one can use it without a key unless that check is switched off.
entries.notes: The boot check was read on the default branch and confirmed present at the v1.105.1 tag; the first release that shipped it was not confirmed, and older releases were not read. The admin web UI was not checked. The published Postgres and Prometheus ports belong to the example compose file, not to the proxy itself.

entries.listen_container: 0.0.0.0 (LLAMA_ARG_HOST=0.0.0.0 in the server stage of .devops/cpu.Dockerfile; the README's Docker example also passes --host 0.0.0.0)
entries.other_defaults: The built-in web UI is enabled by default (--webui) and the slots monitoring endpoint is enabled by default (--slots).
entries.out_of_the_box: Run directly, only programs on the same machine can use it; in the project's own container image, anyone who can reach the published port can use the API and the web UI without a key.
entries.notes: Only the CPU Dockerfile was read; the CUDA and other variants were not.

entries.credential_options: API keys via LOCALAI_API_KEY or API_KEY (empty by default), or its user database
entries.other_defaults: The web UI is on by default (DisableWebUI default false). LocalAI refuses to start on a public address, or on a wildcard address when the host has a public interface, unless API keys or its user database are set up or LOCALAI_ALLOW_INSECURE_PUBLIC_BIND is set; loopback, RFC 1918 LAN, ULA, link-local and CGNAT (Tailscale) addresses are accepted without any credential.
entries.out_of_the_box: On an office LAN it starts without a key and anyone on the network can use its API and web UI; it refuses an unauthenticated start only on public addresses.
entries.notes: The public-address rule is taken from the flag's help text and the call site in run.go; the body of the check (requireAuthOrTrustedBind) is in another file MV2 did not read.

entries.credential_options: none on the server; the FAQ describes no server login or API key, and the OLLAMA_AUTH setting signs the client's own requests rather than making the server demand a credential
entries.out_of_the_box: Run directly, only programs on the same machine can use it; in the official container, anyone who can reach the published port can send prompts and manage models, because the server never asks for a credential.
entries.notes: Ollama does not keep a history of prompts on the server, so reaching it lets someone use the models rather than read earlier prompts; front ends that connect to it are where history is stored. The desktop apps' 'expose to network' setting was not checked.

entries.listen_container: 0.0.0.0:8080 (the image runs the same start script)
entries.credential_options: accounts with admin, user and pending roles; API keys are off by default (ENABLE_API_KEYS=False)
entries.signup_default: open but held: ENABLE_SIGNUP=True and DEFAULT_USER_ROLE=pending, so a new account waits until an admin activates it
entries.other_defaults: ENABLE_ADMIN_CHAT_ACCESS=True (an admin can read any user's chat); ENABLE_ADMIN_EXPORT=True; ENABLE_COMMUNITY_SHARING=True (the share dialog can upload a chat to the Open WebUI Community site); USER_PERMISSIONS_CHAT_SHARE=True with public sharing off. These are stored settings: after the first start the values in the admin panel win over the environment.
entries.out_of_the_box: Anyone who can reach port 8080 can request an account, but sees nothing until an admin approves it; every admin can read every user's chats, and any user can upload a chat to an outside community site from the share dialog.
entries.notes: The image's own Dockerfile was not read; the listen address comes from start.sh, which it runs. The docs say ENABLE_ADMIN_CHAT_ACCESS only governs the interface, and admins can still reach chats through the database or server.

entries.listen_container: 0.0.0.0:30000 on the host's own network (docker/compose.yaml passes --host 0.0.0.0 and uses network_mode: host)
entries.credential_options: --api-key (default None), also used by the OpenAI-compatible API; --admin-api-key (default None) for admin endpoints, which then do not accept --api-key
entries.out_of_the_box: Run directly, only programs on the same machine can use it; with the project's compose file, anyone who can reach port 30000 on the host can use it without a key.
entries.notes: The host and api_key defaults were read on the default branch and at the v0.5.21 tag and match. The compose file is the project's example; the default command of its published image was not read.

entries.listen_direct: 127.0.0.1:7860 (without --listen the Gradio server name is left unset, and Gradio falls back to GRADIO_SERVER_NAME or 127.0.0.1)
entries.listen_container: 0.0.0.0 (docker/nvidia/Dockerfile starts it with --listen; docker/nvidia/docker-compose.yml publishes 7860 and 5000 on every host interface)
entries.credential_options: --gradio-auth or --gradio-auth-path (username:password pairs) for the web UI; --api-key and --admin-key for the API, which runs only with --api
entries.signup_default: no accounts: the web UI has no login unless --gradio-auth or --gradio-auth-path is given
entries.other_defaults: The program prints a warning when --listen or --share is used without either auth option; --share creates a public URL.
entries.out_of_the_box: Run directly, only the same machine can use the web UI; in the project's NVIDIA container, which starts with --listen, anyone who can reach port 7860 can use it without a login.
entries.notes: Only the NVIDIA Docker variant was read. The Gradio fallback address was read from Gradio's default branch, not the version the project pins. Where chat history is kept and who can browse it from the web UI was not checked.

entries.listen_direct: all interfaces, port 8000 (--host has no default and the launcher binds (args.host or "", args.port))
entries.credential_options: --api-key or VLLM_API_KEY, which the docs say covers only endpoints under /v1, /v2 and /inference (the security page adds /cohere); other endpoints, including /invocations, stay open
entries.other_defaults: The docs advise not to rely on --api-key alone and to put an allowlisting reverse proxy in front.
entries.out_of_the_box: Started with no options it answers anyone on the network without a key, and even with a key set some inference endpoints remain open.
entries.notes: vLLM's quickstart says the server starts 'at http://localhost:8000', which is the address to open, not the bind address; the launcher code binds the empty host, meaning all interfaces. The project's container image was not checked.
